target: Q-Explorer (QMS RPV CH) prototype — http://127.0.0.1:8099/index.html · Round 2: open a finished evaluation, read the figures, break them down, check a chart, drill into raw data, export

checked.item: real Chromium (Playwright, /usr/bin/chromium-browser, headless, 1440x900). Login dismissed via button.btn-login and asserted (getComputedStyle(#view-login).display === 'none') before every walk — an earlier run silently failed to log in and produced a bogus tab order, so every result below is from a login-asserted session. Method: DOM-order inventory per view, then full Tab cycles to wrap with document.activeElement + computed outline/box-shadow readback, plus locator.ariaSnapshot() for accessible names. The state map records focus behaviour only for the chart popup, so all other focus evidence is browser-observed.

full Tab cycle to wrap — 90 stops: 4 footer util-links, CSV Export, rpt-aufschluss-1/-2/-3, 2 checkboxes, 'info sheet' link, then 71 row icon buttons (30 Chart, 30 Raw data, 11 Toggle lines), then topbar nav ×5, lang select, Log out. Focus ring visible at every stop (outline auto 1–3px or box-shadow). Zero stops route back to the evaluations list: see A11Y-2.
breadcrumb 'Evaluations' — SPAN.page-bc-link, onclick="showView('reports-list')", tabIndex −1, no role. Never focused in the 90-stop cycle.

2 filter checkboxes ('Reduced connection time (25%)', 'Connections without real-time data') — no id, no <label>, no aria-label, no title, no placeholder: accessible name is EMPTY, a screen reader announces only 'checkbox, not checked'. Real defect, dropped for the 4-finding cap.
expandable param chips (37 TU's / 17 Kantone) — SPANs with onclick, tabIndex −1, no role, no aria-expanded. Mouse-only, but they open read-only lists, so no task is blocked; not reported.

full Tab cycle to wrap — 50 stops: topbar ×5, lang, Log out, util-links, CSV Export, fa-ub-tu-sel, fa-ub-metric-sel, fa-mask-ub-camera, fa-auf-1/-2/-3, fa-add-1/-2, one unlabelled INPUT, 2 info-sheet links, and the row Chart / 'Cancellation mask' / expander buttons. No Close button, no focusable breadcrumb: same trap as V5 (A11Y-2).
full Tab cycle — CSV Export, Close, punct-auf-1/-2/-3, then the row Chart / Raw data / Toggle-lines buttons. V11 is the ONE report view with a keyboard-reachable exit (a real <button>Close</button>).

row action buttons — locator.ariaSnapshot() of the Total row returns: cell "bar_chart table_chart" → button "bar_chart", button "table_chart". The title="Chart"/"Raw data" attributes are overridden by the icon-ligature text content: see A11Y-4.

bundle expander button.punct-expand-btn (title='Toggle lines', content 'expand_more') — no aria-expanded, no aria-controls; the accessible name is 'expand_more' and never changes with state, and the state map records the icon never changing either. Real defect, dropped for the cap.
#punct-chart-overlay — opened by Enter on a row's Chart button. Interrogated for role, aria-modal, focus-on-open, containment, Escape and tabs-to-first-control: see A11Y-1.

toolbar buttons — 6 focusable buttons whose accessible names are the icon ligatures: 'photo_camera' (title Snapshot), 'add', 'remove', 'fullscreen', 'home', 'close'. Same naming defect as A11Y-4; folded into A11Y-1's scope, not double-reported.

16 column search inputs — no id, no <label for>, no aria-label, no title; every one carries the same placeholder 'suchen', so all 16 share one identical accessible name with no column association (verified against their column headers: Trip date, BAV line, TU line, Trip ID, Meas. point, Sched./Actual/Delta BAV+TU arr./dep. …). AUTO-5 already reports them as dead; the naming defect is dropped for the cap.
table semantics — 36 real <th> cells (good), but 0 carry scope, no <caption>, no aria-label on the <table>. Medium at best; dropped for the cap.
#punct-raw-pp rows-per-page <select> — no <label>, no aria-label, no title: accessible name empty, a screen reader announces only the current value. Dropped for the cap.
Close button — a real <button>, tabIndex 0, reachable at Tab 1 from the top of the view. The raw view is keyboard-exitable.

sidebar .nav-item ×3 (Evaluations / New Evaluation / Scheduled Reports) — DIVs, tabIndex −1, no role, visible (display:flex) while a report is open. Already reported as round-1 A11Y-3; re-verified here because it is why the report views have no exit.

topbar nav a.topbar-nav-item ×5 (Startseite, Q-Explorer, Q.Reports, Fotoalbum, Q-Messungen) — focusable with a visible ring, but every one is href="#" onclick="return false". They are tab stops that do nothing, so they are not an escape route from a report.
focus on view change — measured three transitions by keyboard (Anzeigen→report, Raw data→raw view, Close→report): see A11Y-3.

aria-live / role=status / role=alert regions — ZERO in the entire document (querySelectorAll('[aria-live],[role=status],[role=alert]').length === 0), so the 'Preparing CSV export…' snackbar that is the only feedback for the export step of this round's task is never announced. Real defect, dropped for the cap.

gaps: Ausfallmaske V10: I confirmed programmatically that it contains zero Close/Schliessen buttons, but I did not run a full Tab cycle inside it, so its keyboard-exit status is inferred from the same markup pattern as V5/V8 rather than walked.
view-raw-connection: not exercised (the state map lists it as structurally identical to view-raw-punct); its column-input naming is assumed, not measured.

view-chart-punct / view-chart-connection / view-chart-fa full-page chart views: never reached — the row Chart button opens the #punct-chart-overlay popup instead, so those three views' keyboard behaviour is unknown.

Screen-reader announcements were computed from the browser's ARIA tree (locator.ariaSnapshot + accessible-name inspection), not verified with a real screen reader (NVDA/VoiceOver); announcement wording may differ by AT.
Trip-cancellation request flow (fact_check icon per row on V8) was not operated by keyboard, so whether the row's state change is announced is unverified.

findings.element: Chart popup — #punct-chart-overlay (opened from any row's 'Chart' button in view-report-punct); toolbar Snapshot / zoom + / zoom − / fullscreen / home / close
findings.finding: The chart overlay is a plain div with no role and no aria-modal that never receives focus, never contains it and never closes on Escape: after Enter on the trigger, focus stays on the trigger behind the overlay, the next 8 Tabs all land on background table buttons the overlay is covering, it takes 41 Tab presses to reach the overlay's own first control, and Escape leaves it open.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user who opens a chart — an explicit step of this round's task — is left focused behind the overlay, tabs blind through 40 hidden background buttons before reaching the zoom or close controls, and cannot dismiss it with Escape at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Give #punct-chart-overlay role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and an accessible name, move focus to the modal (its heading or close button) on open, trap Tab/Shift+Tab inside it, close it on Escape, and return focus to the row's Chart button on close.

evidence.action: Focused the first row's Chart button (button.punct-act-btn[title="Chart"]) and pressed Enter, then Tab ×8, then counted Tabs to the first control inside #punct-chart-overlay, then pressed Escape
evidence.observed: Overlay opened (#punct-chart-overlay.open, position:fixed, z-index 900, role=null, aria-modal=null). activeElement after Enter was still BUTTON.punct-act-btn[title=Chart] — focus never entered. Tabs 1–8 = table_chart / expand_more / bar_chart / table_chart … all inOverlay:false, view=view-report-punct. First stop inside the overlay came at Tab 41 (BUTTON title="Snapshot"). After Escape the overlay was still present and open.

findings.element: view-report-connection (V5 Anschlusspünktlichkeit), view-report-fa (V8 Fahrtausfälle) and view-ausfallmaske (V10) — the breadcrumb 'Evaluations' (span.page-bc-link, tabIndex −1) is the only route back, and none of the three has a 'Close' button
findings.finding: Three of the report views have no keyboard-reachable way back to the evaluations list: the breadcrumb is a SPAN with onclick and tabIndex −1, the sidebar nav items are DIVs with tabIndex −1, the five topbar nav links are all href="#" onclick="return false", and unlike V11 and the raw view these three ship no Close button.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard user who opens a Connection-Punctuality or Trip-Cancellation report is stranded in it — the only tab stop that leaves the screen is 'Log out', which ends the session, so they cannot go back and open the next evaluation.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the breadcrumb link a real <button> (or <a href>) in the tab order on every report view, and add the same 'Close' button that V11 and view-raw-punct already have to view-report-connection, view-report-fa and view-ausfallmaske.

evidence.action: Opened V5 and V8 by their real 'Anzeigen' buttons, blurred, then pressed Tab repeatedly until the cycle wrapped to stop 1
evidence.observed: V5 wrapped after 90 stops, V8 after 50. Neither cycle contained the breadcrumb, any sidebar nav-item, or any Close button — V5's stops were CSV Export, 3 breakdown selects, 2 checkboxes, an info-sheet link, 71 row icon buttons, then topbar nav ×5 (all href="#" onclick="return false"), lang select, Log out. Programmatic count of Close/Schliessen buttons per view: view-report-connection 0, view-report-fa 0, view-ausfallmaske 0, view-report-punct 1, view-raw-punct 1. Breadcrumb: <span class="page-bc-link" onclick="showView('reports-list')"> tabIndex −1, role null.

findings.element: Every view transition in the read-a-report flow — 'Anzeigen' → report, row 'Raw data' → view-raw-punct, 'Close' → report
findings.finding: Activating a control that swaps the view leaves document.activeElement on <body> instead of moving focus into the new screen, and the prototype has no aria-live region or focus target to announce the change.
findings.user_impact: A screen-reader user gets no announcement that the report, the raw-data table or the list has replaced what they were on, and a keyboard user is thrown back to the top of the document and must re-tab past the whole page chrome after every single drill-down step of the task.
findings.suggested_fix: On every showView() transition, move focus to the new view's <h1>/page title (tabindex="-1" plus .focus()) and give the view container role="region" with an accessible name so the change is announced.

evidence.action: Focused button[onclick*="showPunctReport"] and pressed Enter; then focused the row's 'Raw data' button and pressed Enter; then focused the raw view's 'Close' button and pressed Enter — reading document.activeElement after each
evidence.observed: All three times the new view rendered correctly (view-report-punct → view-raw-punct → view-report-punct) and document.activeElement was BODY, outside any [id^=view-] container. Document-wide count of [aria-live], [role=status], [role=alert] is 0.

findings.element: Row drill-in buttons in every report table — button.punct-act-btn / .rpt-act-btn (title="Chart" and title="Raw data"), 30 of each in view-report-punct and view-report-connection
findings.finding: The row-level Chart and Raw-data buttons are named by their Material-icon ligature text, which overrides the title attribute, so all 60 buttons on a report announce as either "bar_chart" or "table_chart" with no row context.
findings.user_impact: A screen-reader user hears 30 identical "bar_chart" buttons and 30 identical "table_chart" buttons and cannot tell which line bundle's chart or raw data they are about to open — the drill-down step of the task becomes trial and error.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the ligature in aria-hidden="true" and put the real name on the button, including the row: aria-label="Chart — AAGL Busü 1" / aria-label="Raw data — AAGL Busü 1".

evidence.action: locator('#view-report-punct table tbody tr').first().ariaSnapshot(), plus a full Tab walk reading title and computed name at each row-button stop
evidence.observed: ariaSnapshot returned: cell "bar_chart table_chart" → button "bar_chart", button "table_chart" — the accessible names are the ligatures, not the title values. The V5 tab cycle showed 30 stops named bar_chart, 30 named table_chart and 11 named expand_more, all with title present but ignored.
